abstract: In this paper, the reliability of MOSFETs is investigated, focusing on the effect of UIS characteristics on their safe operating region and lifetime. By constructing a UIS test circuit, simulation is utilized to evaluate the effect of circuit design parameters on the test results, such as the effect of changes in duty cycle and inductance values on avalanche energy. The research test system captures the MOSFET on-resistance variations and verifies them through simulation. The results show that the captured resistance value differs from the manual value by 6%, verifying the accuracy of UIS characterization monitoring. This study provides effective support for improving the reliability testing efficiency of MOSFET devices.

articleTitle: A Coherent Integration Process Performed at Sub-Pulse Level for Interpulse-Intrapulse Joint Frequency Agility Waveform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: With the advancement of waveform generator technology, waveform design has become an active anti-jamming method where frequency agility is a primary approach. While frequency agility serves to enhance the performance of the radar, it concomitantly increases the difficulty of signal processing. Focus on the problem of coherent integration in interpulse-intrapulse joint frequency agility waveform, a novel process performed at the sub-pulse level is proposed, which is based on modified non-uniform discrete Fourier transform. In addition, velocity estimation waveform design is introduced to solve the range cell migration and velocity blurring. Simulations illustrate that this process has a good performance on moving target.

articleTitle: Branch-Target Correlation to Resolve Sub-Trace Aliasing in Dead Block Predictor
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: The traditional dead-block predictors have the problem of sub-trace aliasing, leading to unbounded wrong predictions. We believe that by including the information of execution footprints after the last touch, we can better deal with the sub-trace aliasing problem. This paper presents a new method, namely branch-target correlated dead-block predictor (BT-DBP), which adds the correlation of branch targets after the last touch to a memory address as a suffix to a DBP signature to unravel the sub-trace aliasing in a global prediction table. The results show that BT-DBP can reduce the misses incurred in using a global prediction table by 51% on average without scarifying the correct prediction coverage.

articleTitle: Exploring Large Models: From Architecture Innovation to Application Dilem
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: This paper examines large models, crucial role in AI advancements, reviewing their history with a focus on architectural innovations and challenges. Comparative analysis and case studies reveal performance boundaries and scenarios, showing architecture's role in enhancing performance and identifying issues. It provides theoretical references for large model development and application optimization, summarizing trends and their impact on artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Circuit Board Chip Based on Infrared Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: To solve the problems of defect localization difficulty and poor diagnostic effect of the current circuit board chip-level fault diagnosis methods, this paper proposes a circuit board chip fault diagnosis model composed of one-dimensional convolutional network (1D-CNN) and two-dimensional convolutional network (2D-CNN) in parallel based on the infrared temperature sequence. Firstly, the temperature data of the circuit board chips under different failure modes is collected using an infrared thermal camera. Then, 1D-CNN and 2D-CNN networks are used to extract the temporal and spatial features of the data, respectively, for fault information mining. Finally, the defect characteristics obtained from the dual channels are assigned weights and fused using the attention mechanism, before being fed into Softmax for defect classification. The experiment employed a power supply circuit board for conducting reliability analysis. The experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm analysed in this paper has a diagnostic accuracy of 98.73%. Furthermore, the algorithm outperforms the comparison algorithm in terms of stability and reliability.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Interactive Graph Convolutional Networks for Traffic Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Traffic flow prediction, as an important component of smart city construction, plays a crucial role in urban development. Capturing the temporal periodicity and spatial heterogeneity of traffic data is the key to accurately predicting traffic flow. In recent years, many studies have used graph neural networks (GNN) to model and overcome the shortcomings of traditional linear models by extracting spatial features. Additionally, by introducing attention mechanisms, they capture the spatial dependencies and temporal dynamic correlations of different road traffics. However, existing methods typically use separate components to capture spatial-temporal correlations, neglecting the dependencies among various dimensions. To address this challenge, we propose a new traffic flow prediction framework, Spatial-Temporal Interactive Graph Convolutional Networks (STIGCN). By introducing a triplet attention mechanism, the model alternates the use of temporal, spatial, and feature dimension attentions to learn both long short-term and spatial-temporal features. This model eliminates the indirect correspondence between dimensions and weights, enhancing feature expression among dimensions. This paper benchmarks the proposed model on two real-world datasets and achieves good prediction performance in comparative experiments with other baseline models.

articleTitle: Using EEG Data to Classify Hand Motor Imagery in Stroke Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: EEG-driven brain-controlled prosthetics can greatly help people with movement disorders in their daily lives. Still, the task of accurately translating intentions into expected actions in the brain remains a technical challenge. In recent years, as a branch of machine learning, Deep Neural Networks (DNN) have made great progress in improving the recognition and classification ability of computer vision tasks. This study evaluate the information representation ability of 2 machine learning models and 16 NN models and their variants. The experiment is conducted on an open source EEG dataset of hemiplegic stroke patients, and we evaluate the thematic and cross-thematic performance of the above algorithm. We find that a single-layer GRU network remained an optimal choice in subject subject classification because it is able to effectively reduce model overfitting. For cross-subject analysis, some deep-learning models outperform all other methods due to the availability of training data and can function effectively in cross-subject decoding tasks. Independent Component Analysis (ICA) processing is also proved to be effective for improving the accuracy of classification. These improvements will provide important information for researchers in the field of Brain-computer interface (BCI) to select data processing strategies appropriate for their research tasks, it also lays a foundation for the future research on the interaction between the characteristics of bioelectric signals and the structure of neural networks.

articleTitle: Review of Coverless Image Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Traditional image steganography techniques have revealed many drawbacks due to advancements in steganalysis and steganalysis detection technologies. With the continuous development and improvement of various generator-free models, more and more researchers are shifting their focus to the combination of image generation models and steganography techniques. Compared to traditional methods, generative steganography directly drives the secret information to generate images containing the hidden data, exhibiting better resistance to detection against existing statistical feature-based steganalysis. This paper describes and analyzes GAN-based steganography algorithms as well as the latest steganography algorithms based on diffusion models and deep generative models. At the end of the paper, current issues in generative steganography are discussed, along with future research and development directions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Urban Traffic Forecasting with Scalable, Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Accurate traffic forecasting is crucial for managing urban congestion and reducing delays. With the expansion of urban areas, traditional traffic prediction models increasingly struggle to adapt to the complexity and variability of modern traffic patterns. This study introduces a novel approach that leverages deep learning models trained through federated learning across distributed edge devices and cloud servers, such as traffic sensors, to predict traffic patterns. The use of federated learning techniques enhances prediction performance while preserving data privacy. To address the resource constraints and communication overhead associated with federated learning, techniques such as model compression, federated averaging, and selective participation are employed. The proposed approach provides a scalable, efficient, and privacy-preserving solution for accurate traffic predictions in smart cities, facilitating proactive traffic management and urban planning.

articleTitle: Practice and Reflection on Informationization Data Governance in Colleges and Universities
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: This article summarizes the practice and thinking of the Information Office of China Agricultural University in the field of university data governance. The article first elaborates on the background and necessity of data governance, then introduces the goals and framework of data governance, and details the specific practices of data platform construction and data application development. The article also explores the challenges encountered in the process of data governance, including the implementation of data security, the expansion and integration of data sources, the application of data by business departments, and the gradual improvement of data governance work. Finally, the article emphasizes the importance of data governance in the informationization construction of universities, and puts forward prospects for future data governance work. Through these practices and reflections, the Information Office of China Agricultural University has provided valuable experience and inspiration for data governance in universities.

articleTitle: Implementation of RapidIO Driver in Linux Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: RapidIO is a packet-based interconnect technology that provides high performance, high bandwidth, high reliability, and flexible topology, primarily used for system interconnection in the embedded field. This paper designs and implements a RapidIO controller driver for the Linux operating system, with a meticulously designed DMA module to enhance data transfer efficiency and reliability. The stability and reliability of the driver were validated through a QEMU-based testing method. Experimental results demonstrate that the driver is stable, reliable, and flexible, making it adaptable to various application scenarios, and proving its feasibility in practical applications.

articleTitle: Bi-Order Graph Attention Neural Network with Neighbor Node Correlation Embedding for Link Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Node classification and link prediction attracts much attention in network topology analysis. By forecasting the potential presence of a connection between two nodes in a network, link prediction has extensive applications in areas such as power grid management, forecasting, and security. Recently, Graph Neural Network (GNN) based link prediction methods have effectively leveraged deep learning techniques for link prediction tasks and have garnered significant attention. However, many GNN-based approaches focus on feature extraction from the adjacency matrix for embedding at a single scale based on the entire graph structure. In many scenarios, the presence of a link between two nodes is influenced not only by the nodes themselves but also by potential conflicting links among their neighboring nodes at various scales. Thus, incorporating the effects of links and nodes across different scales within the graph is crucial for accurate link prediction for a given node pair. Furthermore, while heuristic information is frequently used as embedding features in link prediction, its integration into GNN-based methods has been relatively limited. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Bi-order Graph Attention Auto-Encoder with Neighbor Node Correlation Embedding (BGAEN) for link prediction. BGAEN enhances graph node features by integrating heuristic information. Additionally, BGAEN incorporates a node correlation-based graph auto-encoding loss to embed heuristic correlation features into node representations. These extracted correlation of node representations are then utilized into a bi-order graph attention neural network as the encoder to capture features across multiple neighborhood scales to alleviate the conflict risk for link prediction. Experimental results show that the BGAEN approach outperforms traditional link prediction methods. The experiments also confirm the effectiveness of the multi-scale neighborhood information and node correlation embedding designed in BGAEN.

articleTitle: Semantic-Based Detection of Ponzi Smart Contracts: Enhancing Bytecode Analysis with Source Code
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: The rapid development of blockchain technology has led to many innovations, with the widespread use of smart contracts being particularly notable. However, this trend has spawned diverse blockchain scams, including the Ponzi scheme, which takes the form of Ponzi contracts. Due to blockchain users' misunderstanding of blockchain transparency, this scam can often result in significant financial losses. To complicate matters further, the vast majority of smart contracts deployed on blockchain networks are not open source, and users can only see the contract's bytecode. This situation makes Ponzi contracts even more challenging to identify, making it difficult for users to judge the security and legitimacy of a contract beforehand, thus increasing the risk of being defrauded. Most existing work uses only bytecode for detection and cannot fully utilize the corresponding source code information. In this paper, we propose a novel bimodal learning-fusion framework for enhancing Ponzi contract detection only in the presence of bytecode. Firstly, we employ the semantic-aware neural network to extract semantic feature from source code and bytecode. Then, we propose a modal transformation strategy to learn the relationship between source code and bytecode. Finally, a modal attention mechanism is introduced to construct a fusion representation to detect the contract even in the absence of source code modality. Experimental results show that the method performs better than existing methods that use machine learning for detection of Ponzi contracts.

articleTitle: Ru-PCFG: Password Guessing Model Combining PCFG and Word Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Passwords are widely used to protect users' data security. How to improve the strength of passwords is significant research since passwords are so easy to hack. Password guessing models are effective for evaluating password strength and improving password security. Traditionally, in common password guessing models, such as the probabilistic context-free grammar (PCFG) model, the focus has always been on simple passwords using only alphabets or digits. Complex passwords will inevitably be a critical study since websites recently require passwords composed of multiple character types. However, the PCFG model has failed to deal with complex passwords; dividing passwords into multiple segments based on character type could reduce their generation probability. To tackle this issue, we propose a new approach, the Ru-PCFG model, which analyzes the transformation of complex passwords from the word level for the first time. This model can detect “transformed words” transformed from words and composed of multiple character types in passwords, restoring them into words and word transformation rules. The results show that about 3% of the passwords in this paper's datasets contain transformed words. By applying the word transformation rules to all alphabet segments during generation, the Ru-PCFG model's guessing success rate can be improved up to 5% for same-site guessing compared to the PCFG model. The guessing passwords are more complex and diverse.

articleTitle: Adaptive Lion Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Solving Small-Scale CVRP
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: An adaptive lion swarm optimization(ALSO) algorithm was proposed for the small-scale capacitated vehicle routing problem(CVRP). The algorithm introduces a nonlinear factor to achieve adaptive scaling adjustment of the perturbation factor, and then dynamically adjusted the search range through the adaptively scaled disturbance factor, enhancing the algorithm's global search capability and local search accuracy. Meanwhile, the position updating strategies for the lion king, lioness, and cub in the algorithm were redefined, with the lioness's position updating strategy incorporating the golden ratio to achieve a more efficient simulation of predatory behavior. Experimental results on standard test cases showed that the algorithm demonstrated good stability and robustness in the optimization process, quickly finding better solutions. Its performance was significantly better than PSO, BBPSO, and LSO algorithms, providing a new solution approach for the small-scale CVRP.

articleTitle: Design of an Electricity Knowledge QA System Incorporating Engineering Ethics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel electricity knowledge question-answering (QA) system that integrates engineering ethics analysis into technical decision-making for the power sector. The system leverages a pre-trained large language model (LLM), fine-tuned using P- Tuning, to address complex queries involving both technical and ethical dimensions. The model parses user queries, retrieves relevant technical information, and performs a comprehensive ethical analysis across four key dimensions: technical, benefit, responsibility, and environmental ethics. Experiments demonstrate the system's high technical accuracy and robust ethical compliance, significantly outperforming traditional knowledge retrieval systems. The results highlight the system's ability to balance technical solutions with ethical responsibility, offering a powerful tool for power system planning, operation, and maintenance. Future work aims to improve the system's handling of socially sensitive ethical issues and enhance its continuous learning capabilities through user feedback.

articleTitle: Research Based on Improved CNN-LSTM Water Quality Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Water quality prediction is an important way to protect water sample area. Most Marine environmental pollution comes from the pollution of shore-based water quality, so the monitoring and prediction of shore-based surface water cannot be ignored. In this paper, the parameters of the model are optimized based on the common water quality prediction models convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory network (LSTM). First, the basic LSTM neural network prediction model is built, and then the CNN model is integrated to make the prediction effect more close to the real value. Secondly, the swarm intelligence algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of the constructed PHz value and ammonia nitrogen prediction model. Finally, the swarm intelligence algorithms such as firefly algorithm(FA), sparrow search algorithm (SSA) and particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) are compared. The SSA-CNN-LSTM neural network prediction model is superior to PSO-CNN-LSTM and FA-CNN-LSTM neural network prediction model, and the SSA-CNN-LSTM prediction model has shorter optimization time and better prediction effect.

articleTitle: Compact and Accurate Binary Neural Network for Real-Time ECG Classification on AIoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Accurate detection of cardiac arrhythmias through electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is critical for timely medical intervention and improving patient outcomes. Despite the proliferation of deep learning-based ECG classification algorithms, many existing models tend to compromise on resource efficiency, resulting in high storage demands and excessive power consumption. This limits their deployment on wearable Artificial Intelligence-of-Things (AIoT) devices, which are increasingly vital for continuous health monitoring. In contrast to conventional binarization approaches, we propose a novel Binary Neural Network (BNN) tailored for ECG signal classification, incorporating innovative basic blocks that enhance both performance and efficiency. Our approach transforms one-dimensional ECG signals into two-dimensional grayscale images, improving data augmentation for small sample sizes. The model achieves a classification accuracy of 97.85<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> with a remarkably compact memory footprint of just 14.07 KB, representing a 31.37-fold compression compared to traditional full-precision models. Furthermore, we introduce scaling factors for both weight and activation binarization, while replacing the ReLU function with the sign function during quantization-aware training. This approach effectively balances model complexity and classification performance. The simplified architecture of our BNN is particularly well-suited for real-time applications, paving the way for its implementation in wearable medical devices, particularly for enhancing patient monitoring and management of cardiac conditions.

articleTitle: RiceDSNet: A Graph-Based Spatial Interaction Model Integrated with BiFormer for Rice Disease Segmentation in natural scene
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Research on rice disease identification has been extensive, but segmentation of rice diseases remains underexplored. Main existing problems include difficulties in obtaining data, complex backgrounds in images, and small lesions. This paper proposes an approach integrating a graph-based spatial interaction module(GSIM) into the vision transformer with bi-level routing attention (BiFormer) called Rice Disease Segmentation Network(RiceDSNet) to achieve accurate rice disease segmentation. To address the issue of complex backgrounds in natural environments, we introduced BiFormer and GSIM. BiFormer's bi-level routing attention(BRA) filters out unimportant information at a coarse-grained level and extracts crucial information at a fine-grained level, thereby enhancing the ability to discern complex backgrounds. GSIM captures relationships between different regions of the entire image, strengthening discrimination across various backgrounds. To tackle the problem of small lesions, we internally integrated cross-layer adaptive fusion module (CAFM) which facilitates the adaptive fusion of “soft” residuals across layers. Finally, the proposed RiceDSNet achieved favorable segmentation results on two individual rice disease datasets as well as a mixed dataset, outperforming other classic segmentation models including FastSCNN and UNet++. The proposed model demonstrated over 4% improvement in disease IoU evaluation across the three datasets.

articleTitle: Implementation of Temperature Prediction and Dynamic Control in Multi-Core Processors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of computer functions and the shrinking feature sizes of processor technology, the number of integrated components on a single processor has grown exponentially. This has led to rising power density and temperature, which in turn affects processor performance, increases leakage power consumption, and even causes permanent failures. On the other hand, as the number of processor cores increases, traditional single-core frequency and voltage reduction methods struggle to handle the complexity of temperature variations in multi-core processors. As a result, ensuring safe temperatures often incurs excessive performance loss. To address this issue, this paper establishes a temperature variation model for processor chips based on a thermal RC model. It also develops power and temperature models for the processor and uses real-time sensor data to predict future temperatures, providing further guidance for temperature control adjustments. The temperature control strategy involves mathematical derivation to predict temperatures and implement more rational frequency and voltage adjustments based on different predicted temperatures. This predictive temperature control algorithm can make adjustments before the processor temperature exceeds the threshold, reducing temperature deviation by 3% compared to traditional reactive temperature control methods. This significantly improves processor stability and safety. Additionally, experimental results under high load conditions show that the temperature prediction accuracy of the algorithm is within 1°C after 1 second and within 2.5°C after 3 seconds, and it can save 1.5% of resources. Finally, this study provides a new solution for temperature control in multi-core processors by predicting temperature changes in advance and dynamically adjusting operational parameters, thereby enhancing processor performance and reliability with practical value.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Design for Quantum Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Processing data through a quantum classifier is a powerful alternative to traditional machine learning. A quantum classifier consists of a series of parameterized quantum circuits that train known quantum data to approximate classification functions and accurately classify unknown data. Considering the development limitations of quantum computers, this paper proposes a kind of lightweight quantum classifier which contains fewer circuit parameters and integrated with the classical optimization algorithm in order to achieve high-precision classification. The architecture design of quantum classifier is inspired on tensor network states such as matrix product state, tree network (TTN) and multi-scale entangled renormalization (MERA), the classical optimization algorithm adopts gradient descent (GD), particle swarm optimization (PSO) and quantum behavior improved particle swarm optimization (QPSO). The whole classical-quantum hybrid model could theoretically be implemented on near-term devices, and its performance is proved on Anderson Iris data set.

articleTitle: Design of an IoT-Based Remote Monitoring System for Injection Molding Machine Clamping Force
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: In order to solve problems such as product flash, tie rod breakage, mold wear, machine damage, and safety accidents caused by inappropriate clamping force applied during the injection molding production process, the article designs and implements a remote monitoring system for injection molding machine clamping force based on the Internet of Things. The system consists of a data collection terminal, a 4G Cat.1 communication module, and a remote server. The data collection terminal utilizes four clamping force sensors to measure the clamping force of the four Green columns of the injection molding machine. The sensor signals are converted and processed using a signal conditioning module and analog input circuit. CH32V307 is used as the microcontroller to collect clamping force information, which is transmitted to the remote server via the 4G Cat.1 communication module. On one hand, the remote server receives and parses data, displaying it on the interface. On the other hand, it stores the data in a database for subsequent querying and analysis of historical data. Threshold parameter information set on the remote server can be fed back to the data collection terminal to complete warning judgment and remote alarm. Test results indicate that the system operates stably with reliable data transmission, enabling accurate remote monitoring of clamping force with a measurement accuracy of up to 0.493%. It effectively improves product quality, enhances production efficiency, and reduces energy consumption.

articleTitle: An Online Visualization Framework for Massive 3D LiDAR Point Cloud Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: The accumulated LiDAR point cloud data is exploding, and its efficient visualization is critical to subsequent point cloud analysis and application. However, due to the large scale of point cloud data, traditional professional point cloud processing software usually has high hardware requirements with low visualization efficiency. Aiming at the problems, this paper designs an online visualization framework for massive 3D LiDAR point cloud data, which allows users to request the resources remotely through the network and interactively visualize the point cloud online in a progressive way. Firstly, the framework proposes a partition method of point cloud data based on the balanced KD-tree and a multi-level storage management scheme to store the point cloud data on HBase. Secondly, an adaptive spatial aggregation query strategy and efficient data transmission protocol based on WebSocket are proposed to support progressive on-demand exchange of massive point cloud dataset. Finally, multiple rendering schemes are designed to realize online visualization of the point cloud. In this paper, the Dutch AHN3 point cloud data is selected for performance validation experiments. Compared with the traditional methods, the online visualization effect is stable and efficient in this paper, and can provide a good interaction experience.

articleTitle: Multi-Scales Hybrid Graph Attention Neural Network with Jaccard Correlation Embedding for Link Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: By predicting the existence of a link in networks, link prediction finds widespread applications in power grid dispatching and security. Recently, Graph Auto-Encoders (GAE) based link prediction methods effectively integrate deep learning into link prediction tasks and attract much attention. However, the existence of a link between two nodes may be closely related to their neighboring nodes in different scales, when GAE-based encoding processes only extract features from the adjacency matrix at a single scale, establishing node features that account for varying influences from different neighborhood sizes becomes challenging. To alleviate this situation, this paper proposes a Multi-scales Hybrid Graph Attention Neural Network with Jaccard Correlation Embedding (MHGAT) to address link prediction tasks. Specifically, MHGAT enhances graph node features by integrating Jaccard Correlation, which reflects the neighboring information, as heuristic information. Then, it designs a multi-scale hybrid attention method for extracting link features around multiple neighborhoods for building a graph encoder to model the importance of nodes. By incorporating a designed node correlation-based graph auto-encoding loss, MHGAT extracts multi-scale neighboring correlation features and leverages these features for link prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to commonly used link prediction methods, the proposed MHGAT approach achieves superior performance. The experiments also validate the effectiveness of the designed multi-scale hybrid attention and node correlation embedding.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fault Diagnosis in Electromechanical Drive Systems using 1D Convolutional Neural Networks and Multi-Sensor Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Numerous existing multi-sensor fusion methods, including data-level, feature-level and traditional decision-level fusion strategies have been implemented for intelligent fault diagnosis in electromechanical drive systems. However, these approaches often are sensitive to poor data quality, ineffective classifiers and focused on single fault types, which leading to reduced accuracy, reliability and robustness of fault diagnosis. To overcome these limitations, this research developed a new intelligent fault diagnostic framework that integrated raw vibration and current data to improve fault diagnostic accuracy, reliability and robustness for electromechanical drive systems in complex fault scenarios. This framework included two enhanced one dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) models optimized for feature extraction and a stacking-based decision-level fusion method that effectively fuses the outputs of these two models. Experimental results showed that this innovative framework achieves an impressive 100.00% average fault classification accuracy across two datasets, significantly outperforming traditional fusion methods. These findings demonstrate the framework's potential to significantly improve the accuracy, robustness and reliability of fault diagnosis in electromechanical drive systems in complex fault scenarios, paving the way for more resilient industrial operations.

articleTitle: Research on Business Capability Evaluation Algorithm Based on Remote Sensing Satellite Ground Receiving System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: With the rapid development of the aerospace industry, the number of remote sensing satellites launched is increasing, and the ground receiving system of remote sensing satellites is facing an urgent need for fast and stable reception of data transmitted by newly launched satellites. In this context, a method for evaluating the business capability of remote sensing satellite ground receiving systems is proposed, and an AHP based business capability evaluation index system is established. Based on the characteristics of the business, the single machine state evaluation model and system business capability evaluation model of the system were elaborated, and the influence weights of each level of factors were determined. The results of the case analysis show that this evaluation method can quickly determine the capability status of the remote sensing satellite ground receiving system for a certain remote sensing satellite data receiving business, provide guidance for system minimization and improvement, and provide feasible suggestions for the utilization and optimization of system resources.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Tool Collaboration Platform for AI Agents
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, AI agents increasingly rely on the collaboration of multiple tools to tackle complex tasks. Existing platforms, however, face significant challenges in tool integration, adaptability, and collaboration efficiency. This paper presents and implements an efficient tool collaboration platform for AI agents, leveraging a modular architecture, standardized interfaces, and rule-based tool adaptation technology. By incorporating core modules for tool management, integration, execution, and data synchronization, along with containerized deployment for environment isolation and scalability, the platform addresses the limitations of traditional systems. Experimental results show that the platform significantly improves tool collaboration efficiency, resource utilization, and system stability, establishing a solid foundation for future AI agent applications across diverse fields.

articleTitle: Development of Monitoring and Calibration System for Vehicle Control Unit of Truck Crane Based on LabVIEW
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: To address the need for real-time data monitoring and online parameter modification during the debugging and calibration of the Vehicle Control Unit (VCU) in an extended-range truck crane, this paper proposes and designs a monitoring and calibration system based on the LabView virtual instrument platform. The system integrates key functionalities, including CAN communication, real-time data analysis, lower-level memory management, and monitoring data recording. It also provides an innovative, efficient calibration solution that eliminates the need for CCP/XCP protocols.Compared to traditional calibration tools, the system features a simplified interface, easy operation, and strong scalability. It enables real-time monitoring of the status of each relay and component within the vehicle. Furthermore, it simplifies the calibration parameter modification process by modularizing key VCU parameters, which significantly improves debugging efficiency while reducing hardware dependence and costs.The system was verified in actual vehicle tests, focusing on high-voltage power management and torque control functions. The results demonstrate that the system exhibits excellent reliability, real-time performance, and scalability, with broad engineering application prospects.

articleTitle: An Architecture for UUV to undertake the Edge Computing in Underwater Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Due to the limitations of marine environments and underwater communication technologies, underwater unmanned energy storage stations (UESS) deployed in distant seas often struggle to leverage shore-based center for complex service computations. To ensure the real-time and accuracy of service calculations of stations, the collaboration of edge computing with cloud computing becomes necessary. This paper presents one architecture with specialized computational underwater unmanned vehicle (UUV) as edge computing devices. It can reduce cost of underwater storage stations and use the power of computing ability fully. Thereby it has the advantage of decreasing energy consumption and facilitating deployment. Additionally, this computing UUV can transmit mass data transmitting between underwater unmanned energy storage stations and shore-based centers as intermediary.

articleTitle: VINS-Integrity: An Integrity Monitoring Scheme for Visual/IMU Integration Based on Factor Graph Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Visual/Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) integrated navigation has garnered significant attention for its superior performance in complex environments. A great deal of research has focused on how to improve the accuracy of Visual/IMU integrated navigation in complex environments, while insufficient attention has been paid to its navigation integrity in the presence of faults. Integrity is an important safety metric for evaluating navigation performance. Compared with the filtering methods, the Visual/IMU integrated navigation system based on factor graph optimization (FGO) has the advantage of higher accuracy but lacks an effective integrity monitoring scheme. In this paper, we propose an integrity monitoring scheme for FGO-based Visual/IMU integration, including Fault Detection and Exclusion (FDE) and Protection Level (PL) capability. Simulation and field experiments were conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. Experimental results indicate that the devised FDE method effectively excludes faulty measurements, and the proposed PL overbounds the position error by 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in all three fault modes.

articleTitle: Siamese YOLO V5 with Structure coefficient for object-level change detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Change detection is a task to identify the location and category of change objects in the reference image and the test image within a specific time interval, that can reduce workload and increase efficiency and reliability in applications such as foreign object intrusion, equipment status monitoring, building or natural resource monitoring, military anomaly monitoring, and so on. To deal with the complicated noise such as dithering, weather, lighting, shadows and background noise in the actual situations, this research combined the Siamese network in conjunction with advanced object detection for object-level change detection. The Siamese network with Structure coefficient is used to extract the fusion difference information between the reference image and the test image to be measured to resist the registration error and unrelated interference between images, which is used to detect the effective rectangular boxes and category of the change objects. Four public datasets of different scenes include LEVIR-CD, VL-CMU-CD, AICD-2012 and CDNET-2014 are used in multiple comparative experiments, and the experimental results proved that our method achieved higher accuracy than existing object-level methods and less false detections than existing pixel-level methods.

articleTitle: Malicious Request Identification Based on a Hybrid Model of BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: Malicious request identification is a key issue in the field of cybersecurity. Existing methods for identifying malicious requests often face limitations when dealing with unknown malicious requests. To address the problem of current malicious request identification methods being ineffective in recognizing unknown malicious requests, this paper employs N-gram for data preprocessing, uses TD-IDF and logistic regression for feature selection, and extracts key features related to malicious requests to enhance the input information of the model. A hybrid model based on BP neural networks is trained to improve the accuracy of malicious request analysis. Experimental results validate the effectiveness and practicality of this model in identifying unknown malicious requests. This research provides new ideas and methods for the identification of malicious requests, holding significant practical importance for cybersecurity protection.

articleTitle: Research on Fine-Grained Gesture Recognition Based on Improved Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: With the development and application of wireless sensing technology, gesture recognition based on wireless perception has become an important component of human-computer interaction. To address the issues of low accuracy and insufficient lightweight design in fine-grained gesture recognition based on Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), we propose a lightweight improvement scheme for fine-grained gesture recognition. This model is based on the VGG-19 network model, which incorporates the SE attention module while implementing lightweight improvements, aiming to enhance the model's recognition accuracy and real-time performance. First, we use Markov random fields to convert one-dimensional phase signals into two-dimensional feature images, using these feature images as input for the improved VGG-19 model, thereby integrating gesture recognition technology with deep learning models to enhance recognition accuracy. Secondly, by improving the VGG-19 network model, we significantly reduce the model's parameters and computational complexity, thus enhancing the real-time performance of the model in recognizing fine-grained gestures. Finally, the SE attention module is integrated into the VGG-19 network model to enhance the adaptive weight allocation capability of the channels and improve the model's focus on important features. By introducing the SE module, the model gains higher feature discrimination capability in deeper convolutional blocks, which helps to improve the accuracy of gesture recognition. Compared to the traditional VGG-19 model, the improved model reduces the number of parameters by 92.5%, achieving an average gesture recognition accuracy of 97.52%. Experimental results indicate that the improved model effectively enhances cross-domain recognition capability in complex environments, significantly improving the accuracy and real-time performance of fine-grained gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Research on Network Security Traffic Classification and Threat Detection Model Based on Incremental Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer (EIECT)
abstract: According to the data from the Cloudflare 2024 Application Security Report, the current cybersecurity landscape faces numerous challenges. As shown in figure 1 below. The report indicates that nearly 7% of daily traffic is mitigated on average, with more than half attributed to Web Application Firewall (WAF) and bot mitigation measures. Although Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks remain the primary threat, attacks targeting disclosed vulnerabilities (CVEs) are also on the rise, with some vulnerabilities being exploited just 22 minutes after proof of concept is released. Additionally, about one-third of all traffic is automated, with 93% of bot traffic remaining unauthenticated and potentially malicious. API traffic continues to grow, accounting for as much as 60% of all traffic, yet a quarter of API endpoints are improperly tracked and managed. Furthermore, enterprise sites integrate an average of 47 third-party endpoints, significantly increasing potential security risks. These statistics reveal the inadequacies of traditional defense mechanisms in dealing with advanced threats, particularly 0day vulnerabilities and attacks that bypass the latest WAF strategies. Common automated blocking measures, such as IP blocking triggered by high-risk or large-scale scanning activities, can lead to false positives and inadvertent blocks, thereby increasing the workload for operations and analysis teams. Therefore, developing and implementing more adaptive defense strategies to enhance the system's ability to handle unknown threats and reduce the operational burden on security teams is crucial.
